title: F7 — the water surface, round 4. The r3 verdict's biggest_gap: the shoreline fade's width was a function of extinction, so it vanished in the region the game is played in. Round 4 puts a shore band in METRES into the fade and pins the mask.
verdict_this_answers: corpus/90-verdicts/wave1/W1-F7-WATER-r3.json (FAIL at 3, 'keep the change'). Its biggest_gap is GAP-W1-F7-the-shoreline-fade-cannot-act-at-the-provinces-own-starting-k, remedy (a) a shore band in metres mixed with the transmittance term, (b) measure >= 2 regions and declare the pose set, (c) one frame-time reading, (d) RI-VIS04 §8's supersample test.
commit_at_filing: read from `git rev-parse HEAD` at filing; every sweep.json below carries its own commit field and they differ because I banked between runs
what_i_could_not_do: **THE ACCEPTANCE FAILS, AND IT FAILS IN BOTH REGIONS. I AM NOT CLAIMING IT.** The r3 verdict's paired acceptance is `gradient_width_px >= 12` at a declared `water_edge` pose in the Deep Marshes, over a pinned mask, at three thresholds, and `RI-VIS03` M12a clause 3 says a band is met only at the WORST pose in the declared set. Measured, pinned mask, threshold 6: Deep Marshes `edge-b135` r3 1 -> r4 **34**; `edge-b225` r3 2 -> r4 **1**; `edge-b315` r3 8 -> r4 **8**; Western Rootlands `edge-b225` r3 5 -> r4 **1**. The worst pose is **1 px**. The 30/34/33 result at `edge-b135` is real, replicated at all three thresholds, and it is ONE POSE OF FOUR. A critic must not read it as the round's headline and neither do I.

**AND THE WIDTH FELL AT TWO OF THE FOUR DECLARED POSES, INCLUDING IN THE SECOND REGION.** `edge-b225` in the Deep Marshes goes 2 -> 1 and `edge-b225` in the Western Rootlands goes 5 -> 1. These are numbers moving the wrong way against the arm I must beat, they are outside nothing I can call noise, and they are the single most important thing in this file.

**NO BAND CONSTANT RESCUES IT — SO IT IS NOT A TUNING PROBLEM AND I DID NOT PRETEND IT WAS.** At the failing pose `edge-b225` I swept the band and got `r3` (band -> 0) width 3, `band-0.60` width 1, `band-1.20` (shipped) width 1, `band-1.35` width 1. Every band constant reads 1. The uniform IS reaching the fragment and its effect IS monotonic in its own parameter — mean luma 68.267 / 66.408 / 60.999 / 58.947 across those four rows, which is the sanity check that the arm is not vacuous — but the parameter does not buy the gradient back. Evidence: `dm-bandsweep/sweep.json`.

**THE ROUND MAKES THE WATER DARKER EVERYWHERE, AND THAT IS A COST NOT A BENEFIT.** Mean luma over the pinned mask at threshold 6, r3 -> r4: `edge-b135` 51.511 -> 44.495 (-13.6%); `edge-b225` 67.717 -> 60.756 (-10.3%); `edge-b315` 68.603 -> 63.400 (-7.6%); Western Rootlands `edge-b225` 83.784 -> 73.439 (-12.3%). In a drowned marsh the bed under the water is DARKER than the water, so a wider fade means the water reads as more absent, not more like water. The r3 remedy's own preservation clause is 'mean_luma at the deck vista not falling below the round-3 arm's' — **I did not capture the deck vista, and at every pose I did capture the number falls.** I am reporting that as a fail, not as a pending item.

**MY OWN CHANGE BROKE EVERY BROWSER-DRIVEN TOOL ON THE BRANCH FOR PART OF THIS ROUND, AND A SIBLING HAD TO REPAIR IT.** The comments I added sit inside `water.js`'s shader TEMPLATE LITERAL, and this repo's comment style quotes identifiers in backticks; each backtick terminated the literal. `node --check` exited 0 on the broken file. The symptom was `window.__HARNESS never appeared` for every tool on the branch, not only mine. Repaired at commit `cdfb59a8` by a sibling doing branch repair (`BRANCH REPAIR (not T4's file)`), 7 comment lines, backtick -> apostrophe, no logic touched — I have re-read the three code lines and they are byte-identical to what I wrote. Written up as **HAZARDS §26** so the next agent does not repeat it. This cost the fleet time and it was mine.

**NO FRAME-TIME FIGURE IS OBTAINABLE ON THIS BOX, AND I NOW HAVE THE MEASUREMENT THAT SAYS SO RATHER THAN THE FOURTH ROUND OF SILENCE.** Two attempts, two replicates each, `three.render(scene, camera)` with `gl.finish()` forcing completion: at 16 iterations `prefix` read **3703.09 ms/world-pass with a replicate spread of 5605.27 ms**; at 4 iterations it read **9.71 ms with a spread of 7.66 ms**. The spread is of the same order as the mean in both, so no arm-to-arm cost difference can be resolved. `engine.js:9382` already says why in its own words: 'Tier-H. This container is SwiftShader; a wall-clock render time here is a fact about the software rasteriser, not the game (RI-PLT01 §A/T1).' Both perf runs also died on their timeout before covering all three arms. **Unmeasurable, with the number that shows it.**

**THE S52 MATCHED-LUMINANCE NULL DID NOT COMPLETE.** My first calibration searched the wrong way — it assumed more transmittance means brighter, and in a drowned marsh it means darker, so it walked away from the target for three iterations (trans 0.5 -> luma 53.71, 0.25 -> 59.822, 0.125 -> 62.874 against a target of 44.368). I rewrote it to probe both ends and learn the direction, but every run that reached the calibration then hit its own timeout: the only rows I have are `end-lo` (trans 0.02, luma 66.54, target 60.597) at `edge-b225`. **So there is NO null row for round 4 and no claim of mine is protected by one.** The r3 critic's null at k = 4.5 is not transferable because round 4 changes the fade's extent, not its average.

**THE `edge-b045` POSE IS VOID AND ITS ROWS MUST NOT BE READ.** It ran under the first version of my capture protocol, which stepped 8 frames before the water-hidden frame and 22 before the pin and then differenced the two to build the mask — so fourteen frames of canopy drift were counted as water. It is void by my own instrument's later evidence, not by argument: at that pose the `prefix` arm, which IS the mask arm, reported an own-mask delta of **+57.77%** against its own pin. Fixed for every run after it (all captures now go through one `captureAt`). **The declared pose set is therefore 3 of 4 in the Deep Marshes, and M12a clause 1 requires 4 — so every M12 band in this file is INCOMPLETE and fails closed, including the ones that would otherwise pass.**

**THE MASK IS UNSTABLE AT THRESHOLD 4 AND I DID NOT FIX IT, I MEASURED IT.** Taking the pin twice through the identical protocol: at `edge-b135` the replicate delta is **+53.24% at threshold 4**, **+1.18% at 6**, **-1.13% at 10**. So threshold 4 is not a usable threshold on this scene and every threshold-4 row in this file should be discounted. Thresholds 6 and 10 are stable to about 1-2%, and the headline width result holds at both.

**THE BLIND GATE DID NOT RUN.** Re-derived by me this turn, not inherited: `grep -rl 'blind_pair: yes' corpus/ --include=*.md | wc -l` returns **102**; `grep -rln 'blind_status: *run' corpus/90-verdicts/ | wc -l` returns **1**, and the r3 critic established that the 1 is a false positive matching a verdict's own prose about the count being zero. A builder cannot spawn a fresh judge (CLAUDE.md rule 0e puts it with the orchestrator). `blind_status: not_possible`, 0, fail-closed.

**NO `TemporalVar`, A FIFTH ROUND RUNNING, AND NO `RI-VIS04` §8 SUPERSAMPLE TEST.** TemporalVar needs >= 5 stationary frames; the supersample test (remedy clause d) needs a 2x recapture and downsample. Both were displaced by the pose set, the second region and the sort test, and by the box sitting at or over its contention ceiling for most of this round. 0 fail-closed, NOT demonstrated absent.

**I RAN BROWSERS WHILE `node tools/contention.mjs` SAID THE BOX WAS OVER ITS CEILING, AND THE TOOL TOLD ME TO SAY SO.** Readings taken during this round: 4.35, 4.44, 3.70, 4.75 and 3.87 load-per-core against a ceiling of 4.0. Five of my runs were killed by their own `timeout` before finishing, which is why several arms are missing rather than negative.

**I DID NOT WRITE THE DITHER-STIPPLE REFERENCE ITEM.** I opened five frames at close range on both arms and the heavy dotted patterning across the entire water surface that two critics have now named is plainly there — it is the dominant texture of our water at the distance a player stands at. It contaminates `NormalEnergy`, which I report as passing. This is the third round in which somebody has named it and not written it. I did not write it either, and the reason is not a good one: I spent the budget on the fade.
headline: The mechanism the r3 verdict asked for is built and it demonstrably reaches the fragment: the fade's width now has no `k` in it. It buys a 1 px -> 34 px waterline at ONE of four declared poses and it buys nothing or less than nothing at the other three, in both regions, at every band constant I swept. The two things this round settles for good are not the fade: the transparency-sorting objection against keeping round 3 does NOT fire, and the mask defect HAZARDS §25 names is real, is +23% at threshold 10, and would have been inside the numbers if I had not pinned.

the_change.files_touched_beyond_it: none in game/ — round 2's Schlick weight and round 3's depth colour are untouched.
the_change.one: A new uniform `uWaterShoreBandM`, default **1.20 m**, chosen from the field and not by eye: `tools/visual/f7-r4-shoreline-census.mjs` finds 71 of 121 water cells within 120 m of the Deep Marshes deck stand carry a corner shallower than 1.20 m and 72 of 121 carry one shallower than 1.35 m, so 1.20 m spans effectively the whole graded population province.js can express.
the_change.two: Three lines in the fragment stage: `esBandM = 1 - smoothstep(0, max(uWaterShoreBandM,1e-4), esDepthM)` — 1 at the waterline, 0 at the band's edge, **no k anywhere** — then `esShoreT = 1 - (1-esTrans)*(1-esBandM)`, the UNION the remedy asked for ('mixed with rather than replaced by the transmittance term'), then the existing alpha line driven by `esShoreT` instead of `esTrans`.
the_change.three: `customProgramCacheKey` v17 -> `v18-f7r4-shore-band-m`, so no cached program can outlive the source change.
the_change.the_colour_half_is_deliberately_untouche: `esDepth = mix(esDeepCol, esBedCol, esTrans)` still uses extinction alone. RI-WLD10 §10.1's 'water is opaque before it is reflective' is a statement about how much light returns from the column and it is right; RI-VIS04 §9's TELL is a statement about GEOMETRY, and how far a waterline is softened over is a property of the bank's slope, not of how murky the water is. A perfectly opaque pond still does not end in a 1 px step.
the_change.preservation_by_construction_S59_both_ar: At `uWaterShoreBandM -> 0` the band is identically 0 and the line is round 3 EXACTLY — that is the `r3` ablation arm and it needs no shader edit, only a uniform. At `esDepthM >= uWaterShoreBandM`, and therefore at everything on province.js's q = 1 clamp, the band is 0 and round 2's look is preserved through round 3's own preservation property. **I verified the first of those against a SHADER arm rather than trusting the algebra**: `r3` (uniform) and `r3-shader` (the alpha line rewritten to `esShoreT = esTrans`) read luma 51.255 vs 50.991 and width 1 vs 1 at `edge-b135`, and 63.322 vs 62.974 at `edge-b045`. The uniform ablation is exact to within the capture's own drift.

the_instrument_and_what_it_fixed.tool: tools/visual/f7-r4-sweep.mjs, mine, new this round. `node tools/ownership.mjs --for tools/visual/f7-r3-sweep.mjs`, run this turn, reports it claimed by a live piece (`W1-30V`), so I did not edit somebody's ruler mid-measurement.
the_instrument_and_what_it_fixed.1_the_mask_is_pinned_and_the_tool_says_w: HAZARDS §25 / `RI-VIS03` M12a's closing paragraph. ONE mask per pose, derived from the named baseline arm (`prefix` = the round-2 shader), and every arm scored through it. That is the conservative direction: the fix is scored on the pixels the arm it must beat calls water, so it cannot widen its own denominator.
the_instrument_and_what_it_fixed.2_and_the_fix_does_move_its_own_mask_MEA: At `edge-b135`, threshold 10, where the pin's own replicate band is **-1.13%**: `prefix` own-mask delta **-1.66%** (it is the mask arm, so this is the band), `r3` **-0.54%**, `fixed` **+23.24%**, `no-shorefade` **+35.67%**. So round 4's arm moves the mask by 23% — twenty times the replicate band — and every distance measured from that boundary would have moved with it. HAZARDS §25 says report it rather than normalise it away; this is the report.
the_instrument_and_what_it_fixed.3_the_distance_transform_now_measures_th: The r3 critic wrote the caveat its own headline depended on: 'in the Deep Marshes that is reed clumps, not a bank.' Our marsh water is punched full of reed blades and trunks, each a few pixels of non-water in the middle of open water, so a raw distance transform reports '3 px from land' for a pixel in the middle of a lake and the profile's far bins never see open water at all. Distance is now taken from a morphologically CLOSED copy of the pin (dilate 4, erode 4); luma is still summed over the ORIGINAL pin so no land pixel enters a luma figure. Both widths are reported on every row, `shore` (closed) and `shore_raw` (r3-comparable), with the pixel count the closing moved — 9.5% to 12.1% of the mask. **The closed and raw widths agree on the headline** (`edge-b135` fixed: 34 closed, 34 raw at threshold 6) and disagree everywhere the width is small.
the_instrument_and_what_it_fixed.4_every_capture_goes_through_one_functio: The first version stepped 8 frames before the hidden frame and 22 before the pin and then differenced them, so canopy drift entered the mask. Found because the mask arm reported a +57.77% delta against its own pin. All captures now share one pose/hide/step/shot sequence, and the PIN IS TAKEN TWICE so `own_mask_delta_pct` has a band under it.
the_instrument_and_what_it_fixed.5_the_pose_set_is_derived_from_the_world: `RI-VIS03` M12a clause 4 wants a `water_edge` pose with a REAL boundary, and three rounds chose close-ups by eye and the r3 critic opened all three and found no bank in any. So `f7-r4-shoreline-census.mjs` runs offline against the same `WorldField` the engine builds, reproducing province.js:1531-1562's cell arithmetic verbatim, and finds the nearest WATERLINE CELL along four bearings fixed at exactly 45/135/225/315 — 90 deg apart by construction, no freedom to shop. Each pose then verifies with the harness's own `projectPoint` (engine.js:9060, read this turn) that the target landed on screen. **All four Deep Marshes targets and both Western Rootlands targets verified `in_front: true, on_screen: true`.**
the_instrument_and_what_it_fixed.6_it_paints_the_fade_field_itself: `gradient_width_px` reads the SCENE as much as the shader, so two arms `probe-shoreT-r3` and `probe-shoreT-r4` render `esTrans` and `esShoreT` straight into the water surface as greyscale with alpha forced to 1. Tonemapping maps the value but not the ordering, so the spatial EXTENT survives it.

Evidence directories under corpus/90-verdicts/wave1/artifacts/W1-F7-WATER-r4/.

A passing NormalEnergy may be scoring the stipple. `RI-VIS04` §8's supersample test would separate them and I did not run it.

the_fade_field_painted_directly_probe_sh.what_it_says_and_it_cuts_against_me: At `edge-b225` the r3 fade field is almost entirely black (mean 12.1/255, only 16% of the surface in transition) — that IS the k = 4.5 collapse the r3 verdict diagnosed, measured directly for the first time. But at `edge-b135`, where the luma-vs-distance width says r4 is 34x better, the fade FIELD says r4 has LESS transition area than r3 (0.61 vs 0.93) and is more saturated. **The two measures disagree at the pose that carries my only positive result, and I am not choosing between them.**

the_transparency_sort_against_the_wet_ba.why_it_matters: The r3 build's own overturn condition #3 and, in the r3 critic's words, 'the strongest untested argument against keeping the change'.
the_transparency_sort_against_the_wet_ba.sort_state_read_off_the_live_scene_not_a: water plane: `transparent: true`, `depthWrite: **false**`, `depthTest: true`, `renderOrder: 0`, opacity 0.772-0.96 per region. Wet-bank strip (`water:shoreline:*`, province.js:1590, its own `wet_mud` material): `transparent: true`, `depthWrite: false`, `depthTest: true`, `renderOrder: **3**`, opacity 0.74. The strip therefore always draws after the water plane.
the_transparency_sort_against_the_wet_ba.this_corrects_the_r3_status_file: The r3 status says the round 'lowered alpha on a `transparent: true` material with `depthWrite` on'. **`depthWrite` is false on every water material**, by `visual-foundation.js:689` (`depthWrite: options.depthWrite ?? family!=='water'`) and confirmed on all four live materials at runtime.
the_transparency_sort_against_the_wet_ba.reading: The wet-bank strip moves **-1.845 on a base of 44.362 (-4.2%)** while the water it sits on moves **-22.231 on 66.945 (-33%)** — the change is 12x more confined to the water surface than to the bank. The land leak check moves **-0.568 on 76.598 (-0.74%)**, which is inside the capture's own drift (the pin replicate at this threshold is 1.18%). **The overturn condition does NOT fire.** This is a result for keeping round 3 and for keeping round 4's mechanism, and it is the one clean thing in this file.
the_transparency_sort_against_the_wet_ba.the_observation_i_did_not_expect: The whole resident scene at the Deep Marshes stand contains exactly ONE wet-bank strip and it belongs to `eastern-rootlands`. There is no `water:shoreline:deep-marshes` mesh anywhere in frame, despite my census finding 47 waterline cells within 120 m of the stand. I did not chase it — it is province.js's file, not F7's — but it is a candidate defect and it is exactly the kind of absence that `ARBITRATION` S64 says must be carried forward rather than absorbed.

the_premise_in_my_brief_that_i_falsified.what_the_brief_and_the_r3_verdict_both_s: That the Deep Marshes is WCI 0.86 / drowned, that 'all three shoreline close-ups are shoreless', that `distanceFromLand` there 'is measuring reed clumps', and — my brief's own words — that if the region 'genuinely has no shoreline to fade ... the honest move is to say the region was the wrong choice'.
the_premise_in_my_brief_that_i_falsified.what_i_measured: `tools/visual/f7-r4-shoreline-census.mjs`, offline, against the same `WorldField` the engine builds, reproducing province.js's cell arithmetic verbatim. Within 120 m of the `vista-deep-marshes` stand: **121 water cells, 47 of them waterline cells (38.84%), nearest at 17.7 m**, and only **24.16%** of wet corners sit at province.js's q = 1.0 depth clamp — so **76% of the water in frame carries a live depth gradient**. At `eye-deep-marshes`: 144 cells, 51 waterline (35.42%), nearest 25.9 m.
the_premise_in_my_brief_that_i_falsified.the_correction: **The Deep Marshes is not shoreless. It is full of shoreline.** What was true is narrower and is a POSE fact, not a REGION fact: round 3's close-ups were shot at 4.5-7 m from a player standing in open water whose nearest waterline cell is 17.7 m away, so they could not contain a bank at any bearing. Every one of my four declared targets in that region is a real waterline cell with graded corner depths (0.027 m to 1.49 m) and every one verified on screen.
the_premise_in_my_brief_that_i_falsified.where_the_region_argument_IS_right: The two seas are where the depth signal is genuinely dead: Marauder's Coast q-saturation **0.9248** and Crimson Coast **0.9706**, with 4 waterline cells of 121 and the nearest at 81 m and 60.5 m. No shader reading province.js's vertex colour can fade there, at any k, and that is a province.js limit rather than a water.js one.
the_premise_in_my_brief_that_i_falsified.and_a_thing_three_rounds_have_been_doubt: The in-frame HUD region label reads `western-rootlands` on captures taken at the `vista-deep-marshes` stand — the same symptom the r1 F7 critic wrote `tools/visual/f7-critic-deck-region.mjs` to chase. Measured in-process this round: `teleport` landed at exactly [3123.5, 3715] with **offset 0.00 m**, and the RUNNING field's `regionAt` returns `deep-marshes` for both the deck point and the player, with `hud_region_name: 'The Deep Marshes'`. **The field is right and the drawn label is stale.** It is not F7's file and I did not fix it, but three rounds of F7 evidence have been under suspicion because of it and they should not be.

the_ruling_i_made_and_what_would_overtur.ruling: **KEEP the mechanism, and I am NOT claiming F7 or the acceptance.** The change lands with its band as a uniform defaulting to 1.20 m.
why_keep: The defect the r3 verdict named is genuinely removed from the MECHANISM: `esBandM` contains no `k`, so the fade's width is no longer a function of extinction. That is verifiable by reading three lines and does not depend on any measurement of mine.

It is exactly reversible in one number and I proved the reversal rather than asserting it: `uWaterShoreBandM = 1e-4` gives round 3, and a SHADER arm restoring round 3's alpha line independently agrees with it to within the capture drift (51.255 vs 50.991; 63.322 vs 62.974).
The strongest recorded argument against keeping — the transparency sort against the wet-bank strip — was tested for the first time and does not fire.
the_ruling_i_made_and_what_would_overtur.why_a_critic_may_reasonably_overturn_thi: Two of four declared poses get WORSE, the water is 8-14% darker at every pose, and the only pose that improves is contradicted by my own fade-field probe. A reviewer who weights 'the water reads as more absent in the starting region' above 'the mechanism is now correct' should set the default band to 1e-4 and ship round 3's behaviour with round 4's uniform in place. **I considered that and did not do it**, because a default that makes the change invisible would also make it unjudgeable, and the next round needs the numbers this default produces.
what_would_overturn_it: A completed matched-luminance S52 null that reproduces the `edge-b135` width. I could not run one and that alone is enough to hold the result at 'unprotected'.

The deck-vista preservation clause: if `mean_luma` at `c-vista-11-d26` falls below the round-3 arm's — and it fell at all four poses I did take — the r3 remedy's own paired acceptance is failed on both halves, not one.
A blind pair ranking round 3 above round 4. Nobody has run one, ever, for this piece.

Any evidence that the `edge-b135` 1 -> 34 result is an artefact of the morphological closing. The raw width agrees there (34) and disagrees everywhere else, which is a pattern a critic should attack directly.
